policy.description: Blocking line-coverage ratchets. For a fixed scope, coveredLines is the highest value in the reviewed clean-run observation envelope, never a modal or repeated lower value, and that high-water never decreases. Update the envelope in the same reviewed change whenever scope or coverage advances. A fixed-scope floor may move downward only to the exact minimum directly observed by clean runs on the identical source, tests, and total-line scope, with linked evidence and a bounded tolerance; unexplained coverage loss remains a regression.

tolerance.rationale: The issue-682 client changes add critic-rating parsing helpers and OSD/tag-pipeline coverage. Three hosted runs (jobs 92222716772, 92224161396 and 92225613803) passed the complete client test execution and measured the identical 2,811/3,196 (87.954%) high-water on the exact client source and test scope; the first correctly failed only because that new scope had not yet been recorded in this ratchet artifact.

The issue-682 fix preserves direct critic percentages (including zero and single-digit Rotten Tomatoes scores) through every live and full-cache rating-inheritance path and bumps the cache schema to v5 so rows written under the retired CommunityRating-only rule are invalidated. After the semantic repair on current main, four clean coverage runs using the pinned .NET 10.0.9 runtime passed all 4,144 tests on the exact final source, tests, and 53,179-line scope and observed 43,479, 43,475, an independent-review 43,484, and a hosted-CI high-water of 43,485 covered lines (81.771%). The ten-line envelope is timing-dependent branch coverage in the tag-cache monitor's asynchronous invalidation paths, not a source or test difference; the spread is 0.019 percentage points, far inside the 0.15pp policy bound. coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact scope-drift, regression, stale-baseline, observed-high-water, spread, single-run, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.
